findings.claim: The official Node.js process documentation (nodejs.org/api/process.html, which showed v26.11.1 when retrieved) says `process.cwd()` was added in v0.1.8. It says the method returns a `<string>`: "The `process.cwd()` method returns the current working directory of the Node.js process."
findings.falsifier: This would be false if the official `process.cwd()` section at nodejs.org/api/process.html#processcwd gave a return type other than string, or described the value as something other than the process's current working directory. It would also be false if the fetched text did not match the live page.
limitations: The page was read through a WebFetch summarizer, so the quoted text passed through an extraction model. It was not read verbatim in a browser.
Only the latest docs (v26.11.1 at retrieval) were checked. Older or LTS versions of the docs were not compared.
The docs page does not say that the value changes after `process.chdir()`. That caveat comes only from third-party sources and is not part of this claim.
Edge cases are not covered here, such as Windows path format or what happens if the working directory has been deleted.
beta.docs.nodejs.org/process/cwd appeared in search results but was not fetched. It is the same organization, so it would not count as an independent source anyway.

findings.claim: The official Node.js process documentation (nodejs.org/api/process.html, v26.11.1 when retrieved) says `process.version` was added in v0.1.3 and has the type `<string>`. It says: "The `process.version` property contains the Node.js version string." The example output is `v14.8.0`, with a leading "v". The docs say to use `process.versions.node` to get the version without the prepended v.
findings.falsifier: This would be false if the official `process.version` section said the type is not a string or that it does not hold the Node.js version string. It would also be false if the docs did not include the prepended 'v' or the pointer to `process.versions.node`.
limitations: `process.version` is a property, not a function, so it has a Type and does not "return" anything in the sense the brief uses.
Text was extracted via a WebFetch summarizer from the second part of a long page (offset 100000).
v14.8.0 is only an illustrative example value. The docs do not formally specify the version-string format, such as semver or pre-release suffixes.
Only the current docs version was checked. Historical doc versions were not compared.
